edges.description: FAT4, with its ligand Dachsous1, controls planar cell polarity of valve endothelial cells; loss disrupts lymphatic valve leaflet formation.
Defective lymphatic valve morphogenesis and drainage produce dysfunctional lymphatics.
Dysplastic intestinal lymphatics dilate and leak lymph into the gut lumen.
Impaired lymphatic drainage in the limbs, genitalia, and face causes lymphedema.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes serum albumin and immunoglobulins.
Enteric protein loss lowers serum albumin.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes serum immunoglobulins.
Enteric loss of lymph depletes circulating lymphocytes.

nodes.description: Lymphedema, distinguishing Hennekam syndrome from Van Maldergem syndrome, is a core feature; it affects the limbs, genitalia, and face. In the FAT4-related form, lymphedema is often reported to begin later in childhood, in contrast to the frequently congenital lymphedema of the CCBE1-related form, although this distinction is based on limited published cases.

evidence.reference_title: Van Maldergem syndrome and Hennekam syndrome: Further delineation of allelic phenotypes.
evidence.snippet: Both conditions are characterized by a typical facial gestalt and mild to moderate intellectual disability, but differ in the occurrence of neonatal hypotonia and feeding problems, hearing loss, tracheal anomalies, and osteopenia in VMS, and lymphedema in HS.
